Lessons.Title: Exponential Situations as Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning objective: select input and output variables, decide if a relation is a function and write exponential growth/decay in function notation, interpreting the same input-output pair across table, graph and situation. Original Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 5 Lesson 8, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/5/8/preparation.html and student lesson https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/5/8/index.html (CC BY 4.0). Source distinguishes exponential function direction from a reversed relationship that may be logarithmic and is outside current course.

Original fictional social-media test metric: for nonnegative whole days t, suppose a benchmark indicator begins at3 units and doubles daily, F(t)=3·2^t. Values3,6,12,24 at days0–3. Each day yields exactly one indicator output, so t→F(t) is a function. The modeled numbers are not real platform or user analytics.

Now describe input/output roles: input t is elapsed days; output F(t) is units. Function notation F(2)=12 means the metric has12 units after two days under the proposed rule, not12 days after two units. One can ask for a time at which F(t)=12 by inspecting the table; an inverse-time rule for arbitrary outputs is different and need not be taught as another exponential function.

Student task: create a second original exponential relationship from table and graph, identify independent/dependent quantities, explain function uniqueness and test a proposed pair. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 each for domain/units, correct equation/table, function-notation interpretation and comparison with a nonfunction relation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Function assignment
KeyConcepts.Definition: Every allowed input has exactly one output.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Check for repeated inputs with conflicting outputs.

KeyConcepts.Title: Exponential notation
KeyConcepts.Rule: Define output units and input time.

KeyConcepts.Title: Direction of modeling
KeyConcepts.Definition: Which variable is input affects how a relationship is expressed.
KeyConcepts.Example: t→F(t) is exponential; solving for arbitrary t from F may require inverse operations beyond scope.

WorkedExamples.Title: Write function from a table
WorkedExamples.Question: Use values3,6,12,24 at days0–3.
WorkedExamples.Method: Derive the specific first-party mathematical rule, independently verify it and interpret with the stated domains.
Steps: At day0 output3 gives initial a=3.

WorkedExamples.Title: Explain notation in context
WorkedExamples.Question: What does F(2)=12 mean?
WorkedExamples.Method: Derive the specific first-party mathematical rule, independently verify it and interpret with the stated domains.
Steps: Input2 means two days after baseline.
The statement does not reverse input/output roles.
WorkedExamples.Answer: At day2, indicator is12 units under model.

WorkedExamples.Title: Check a disputed point
WorkedExamples.Question: Does pair (3,20) belong to F(t)=3·2^t?
WorkedExamples.Method: Derive the specific first-party mathematical rule, independently verify it and interpret with the stated domains.
Steps: Because values differ, pair is off the graph.
WorkedExamples.Check: Each t has exactly one output.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Reversing input and output in F(2)=12
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The argument inside parentheses is input.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating every reversed correspondence as an exponential function
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Finding an input from a given output is an inverse relation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Check variable roles before naming the model.

SummaryPoints: Exponential functions can be presented through values, graphs, rules and notation.
F(t)=3·2^t assigns one output per allowed day.
Function input/output units must be explicit.
Teacher scores interpretation, not just arithmetic.
